title: Make Learning Permanent
author: Scott Young
description: How much can you remember from your high school classes? If I gave you one of your final exams today, could you still pass it? In their now-famous study, Harry Bahrick and Lynda Hall asked this question of nearly two thousand people. Unsurprisingly, they found what most of us expect: a few years out from […] The post…
summary: How much can you remember from your high school classes? If I gave you one of your final exams today, could you still pass it?
takeaways: Even fifty years later, without any additional rehearsal or practice, they managed to maintain almost exactly the same test performance they had from the start.
Before we look at the factor driving near-perfect memory performance in one of the groups Bahrick and Hall studied, we need to start by recapping how normal forgetting works.
After that, the strength of the memory flattens out; we continue to forget, but at a less rapid rate than before.
